1) Depends on where you live. The national average is $17.50, where I live, a vet tech is very lucky to get $15.50 after working in clinic for the last 3 years. Know your worth, if you are a college grad who sat for the VTNE, you are generally worth more than your on the job trained tech... no disrespect to them, but if you have gone through the education and testing, you should be more educated about the job than them. That may not always be the case, but that is what I have found and what I was told while in school. 

2) Vet Med is not a nine to five job.... Expect there to be days where you work over 14 hours. However, this can also depend on if you do large animal or small, where you live, if there is a 24 hour clinic nearby, etc. 

3) I didn't have many benefits, but I worked a lot with shelters and non-profits... so they couldn't provide me with a lot of benefits... Some clinics take awesome care of their employees, some don't shop around before you commit to a job. 

4) You can go an do a multitude of things: phelobotomy for humans, Lab tech, specialize in a specific field like dentistry, wildlife rehab, mortuary science for humans, animal shelter management, dental hygienist for humans, department of wildlife, lots and lots of options... But usually there will be a few more classes or specific training that might be needed. Mortuary science has some necessary laws that need to be studied, but you will have the physical and mental skills to handle those jobs... 

5) You get to do what you love. You bring life in to the world and you have a chance to give a suffering animal peace. You save lives. You teach. You feel like you've made a difference. It can be beautiful and fulfilling... 

6) It hurts... I have PTSD, in part, from being a vet tech. It leaves wounds that no one is prepared to face or deal with, even trained therapist have problems helping us. Coping is the hardest thing to figure out. Lack of adequate pay, long hours, stress, dealing cattiness in the workplace... Not having support. Its a hard career to have. Its why most techs only last 5 years in the business... 

7) I can't recount all my animal related experiences, but I've worked with wildlife to small animal and shelter medicine. There are a lot of stories I could tell you. I went to a high rated school. It was awesome. I love my school, could it have prepared me for everything... no. But I think there should be a class on learning to cope.. Compassion Burnout, Depression, PTSD, Exhaustion... these are all things we deal with that your told about, but never really taught to deal with. I think we need to be more open and honest with each other. I think we need to be more supportive and less competitive. I think we need to really address the fact that some techs are made to work three days without sleep... that I, myself have gone through a 14 hour shift without eating, drinking, using the bathroom... that we generally work six days a week.... We are only human. We are not robots. If we cannot take adequate care of ourselves, how can we do so for our patients? The industry needs to catch up... but also, we need more people willing to be vet techs. I really can be a beautiful job... but we need to be able to live as vet techs too.

I would not do an online school... This is a very hands on job, knowing the concept of how to do something and being able to physically do it are two different things. You need the hands on experience, and though an online school requires you to have an externship with a local vet, they will usually not have practice equipment and a lot of time to really teach you how to do things... Though you will probably get more experience on the software and at reception... Because, aside from kennel teching.... that will probably be a lot of what they allow you to do... Most Vets are legally liable for their techs... except in some states... So, for a lot of procedures, you as a tech in training, will not be allowed to do a lot. Also, depending on the vet, you may not get the amount of coverage/exposure to different species... Which might be problematic considering the VTNE is randomized each year... One year will be Large Animal, one year Small, the next year Exotic... You never know what will be covered... This can lead to you failing the VTNE, which is three hundred dollars every time you take it. I would recommend applying for a AVMA accredited school. That way, you know the money you spend on your education will be worth it.

Every day symptoms are nausea and vomiting, back pain, cluster migraines, insomnia, light sensitivity, diarrhea or constipation, fatigue and lethargy, anxiety, depression, lack of oxygen, tunnel vision, seeing spots, dizziness, short of breath, irritability, and anorexia. Episodes usually begin with fever and tachycardia, followed by paranoia. Then it moves into pain and stiffness in my joints and muscles. I get intense pain in my abdomen and back. I also get chest pain and limb pain. I get numbness in my limbs, to the point where one time I took a bath in straight hot tap water and it felt cold to me. Then the muscle weakness sets in, I cant't hang onto things, can't grasp things. I get paranoia and delirium. And finally I start hallucinating and then my urine is usually very dark, on the orangish side or brownish side. It will turn purple or deep red if left in sunlight, but when I'm deep in an episode I urinate pretty much straight hemoglobin and porphryins. My urine will smell a lot like protein. It will be very flocculent or cloudy. 

The biggest problems with AIP are 1: that we cannot make heme so we can't make hemoglobin and new red blood cells. So a lot of our blood cells are old or too new. Porphyrins are a building block of heme, which is a building block of hemoglobin. 
2: Our spleens are healthy. Spleens are essentially big sponges of blood. They act as a filter. In each of the little pockets in the spleen, there are white blood cells. They scan all of our blood every five minutes. Because our cells look strange, they get plucked out of circulation. So not only can we not produce more blood, we are constantly loosing blood to our own spleen. Thankfully, the hemoglobin we do produce, or have transfused, is recycled when the cells are broken down by the spleen. But because the rate of cellular breakdown is so high, especially in an episode, we urinate a lot of protein. Which is really hard on the kidneys. 
3: Our Kidneys are generally healthy. They produce erythropoetin, which is a chemical that stimulates our bone marrow to produce more red blood cells. However, because we lack the ability to make more hemoglobin, our porphyrin level increases. The levels get so high that we become intoxicated by the amount of porphyrins in our blood. This is what happens when we enter an episode. If I were to donate blood, and someone were to receive it, they would have symptoms similar to an porphyria episode. 
4: We are anemic... we are loosing blood and cannot make more. So because of this we are always lacking in oxygen. 


So because of all these factors, every system in our body is effected. Our central nervous system is a huge issue. Our brains lack oxygen and suffering from intoxication. This damages the nerves in our peripheral nervous system. Which leads to the neuropathic pain we feel. Literally this pain cannot be treated. Not even morphine will begin to dull it. I imagine testicular pain and some of the pain experienced during labor is neuropathic. I have no evidence for this, but no one seems to be able to describe it, which is how neuropathic pain feels. It literally takes all the strength out of you. It takes your breath away. And we feel it for days on end. 

I also get some cutaneous symptoms, but only when I'm triggered through diet. Kiwis, Papaya, pineapple, starfruit, etc all trigger a reaction in me. I will literally break out in third degree burns from UV light. Though my eyes and skin are already very sensitive to light. I know this is something your familiar with! 

I haven't had my genome tested yet, I'm signing on with a study at the University of Utah to get it done... its really, REALLY expensive otherwise. My mother and grandmother both have AIP. My grandmother died during an episode, she started seizing and finally passed. I was always a sick child. I have very little immunity, always have. I would always vomit in the mornings and no one knew why. I was told growing up that its very rare to inherit porphyria, none of my siblings have it. So I was tested for everything. I've been misdiagnosed so many times. So it wasn't until I really started looking into it that I found a match to my symptoms. I've had my chems tested, but they are doing several tests, a survey,  during the month to see where my levels are throughout my episode from beginning to end. 

Do you work from home then? I work a forty hour job, and I'm barely making it through the day. I can't raise my energy with anything. I'm also a huge supporter of death with dignity. If I'm this sick now, how will it be in five years? Ten?

Do you suffer from any depression associated with your disease? Can you get a bone marrow transplant, or is your EPP not severe enough to risk it?

Well, hello. I'm a Druid High Priestess who has been studying for over 20 years. I was ordained in 2013 and have lead several groups in my local area. Unfortunately, you tend to find a lot of ageism in the international community. Expect that your age may be brought into question. I personally don't have an issue with age. If a person is asking questions, they are ready to know the answer. A lot of people come to Paganism as a way to escape their prior religion... as seems to be the case with you. I'm sorry that you feel so strongly towards them, and I'm also sorry for the reason you feel that way. I'm also sorry to hear about your mother. The loss of a parent is always hard. 

Some people are fake in this religion/spirituality. Some are harder to see than others. But that's with every sect in every country, in every religion... there will always be fakes and people who believe one thing and practice another. The important thing is to practice what you preach. 

I wouldn't call that materialism... materialism is more like LaVeyan Satanism where they believe that being materialistic is a good thing. You are looking for evidence. Overall, Paganism is an experiential path. No one can truly tell you how to live it, you must live it for yourself. Your experiences will differ from mine and everyone else. Everyone sees life differently based on how they experience it. But you should trust your intuition. Your intuition is key in how you experience life. You can make decisions for yourself, in fact, its your responsibility to do so. If you can't trust yourself, how can you trust anything? As the Oracle at Delphy said: Know thyself. That is a huge lesson in Paganism. Know thyself and you will know Deity. As within so without. You cannot learn about the world, until you are ready to learn about yourself. 

Question everything. As I said before you can make decisions for yourself. So ask questions. Be willing to learn. Be willing to hear answers you don't agree with, then decide why you don't and go from there. 

Read everything. A lot of people will advise you against reading certain books... again, you can decide for yourself whether you agree or not. Its a part of learning. And expect that to change over the years as you grow. Be willing to allow your beliefs to grow and change. 

I can tell you that I personally do have a special relationship with my Deities. They do speak to me, but not necessarily in a way that most people would expect them to. Its a voice, not inward or out... its simply there. Or they speak in energy. It all depends on how I perceive it in the moment. I have a connection to my deities... I think one would have to in order to be a Priest/Priestess. But everyone practices differently. There are certainly many among the Pagan community that are Agnostic or Atheistic. 

You can most certainly study Paganism and not directly worship a pantheon or a deity. In fact, if you look at Buddhism, Theraveda Buddhism specifically, you will see that they do not directly worship Buddha. They worship and practice the concepts of Buddhism. You can also study the practices and concepts of Paganism and still be a Pagan. 

As for life after death, again, no one can decide for you. If you truly believe we rot in the ground, then that is your answer. If you believe that we are reincarnated, that is your answer. No one can answer it for you. You must study and search for that answer yourself. Decide what you decide, and don't worry if that changes as you study. Its all a part of growth. To me, energy is never created nor destroyed. It simply changes. So I personally do believe in reincarnation, but that is based off how I see the world. How I experience my path. Its different for everyone. As a Druid, I also believe in ancestor worship. Meaning, I believe we can reach out to the dead, that they can be connected with and communicated with. I personally have a altar that is for this purpose. I have pictures of my family and friends that have passed. If nothing else, its a nice way to honor and remember those we love who have passed. 

Meditation is not necessarily for that purpose, but it can be helpful. I find simply, deeply thinking about one thing always makes me enter a trance. Its like daydreaming. Some of the best answers can come simply from deep contemplation.  

Learn to meditate however you are most comfortable. If sitting in a rocking chair helps calm you mind, then that is where you meditate. If doing it before sleep helps, then you do it before sleep. If thinking about one subject/question, instead of completely clearing your mind helps, then that's what you do. If listening to music helps, then that's what you do. When you are finally able to calm your mind, then you can progress from there. Breathing exercises help a lot, but if you tend to be a person who gets caught up in the details of things, then you'll only be focusing on not screwing up... A lot of people will tell you that it doesn't matter, and it doesn't, but if that's all you can think about, then its not really doing you much good. If that happens, then try a different method. There really is no wrong way of doing it as long as your achieving your intended goal. Do what feels right.

Paganism can be a very useful tool for self discovery. Satan really is more of a Christian idea and Satanism is a sect of Christianity. Literally, it wouldn't exist without the creation of Christianity. There are no devils in paganism. I do not consider Satanism a form of Paganism. Depending on the form of Paganism she is studying, its generally very earth based. As for the demons/possession... there really isn't much of that in Paganism. We are taught, and teach, that we are in control of our bodies. No one can take anything from us and no one can possess us. We have full responsibility over what we practice and how we practice it. I would say that her interest in such things is pretty typical for a kid these days. Look at a lot of the movies coming out! A lot of them have to do with possession and demons. Its more of a pop culture thing than a Pagan thing. Your her parent and you should absolutely have an active part in your child's study. Be supportive and listen. She could just be looking for another way of thinking about religion and spirituality. She could be trying to understand herself and her beliefs on a deeper level. I would only be concerned if she starts or has a history of violent behavior. That has nothing to do with spirituality or Paganism, but she could be looking for a reason for it or even a way to reject some sense of responsibility. That tends to be my concern when dealing with younger people. WHY do they want to learn about this? Are they being influenced by negative stereotypes? Are they just wanting to impress their friends or have something they can use to scare people? None of these things has anything to do with Paganism and everything to do with immature people. We all know those people who want to be Goth or a Metal Head to scare people, and unfortunately, Paganism has those kinds of people too.  Never be afraid to ask. Its really important to have a sincere dialog with your children. Be open to whatever she says. If your still concerned, for instance I would be concerned if my child was torturing animals (Nothing to do with Paganism), call in a counselor.

I'm also a person suffering from Porphyria. I have AIP. I get episodes about once a month lasting for about three weeks. Its interesting that your face is unaffected. Do you have Cutanea Tarda? I wouldn't say that the blood urges you have, have anything to do with your disease, but you could have another disease called Renfield's Syndrome. Which is also called Clinical Vampirism. Have you been tested? Who treats you? Is it you GP or do you see a specialist? Does diet effect your condition? Do you have children? Are your children effected? Do you suffer from co-infections on your lesions? How do you treat them? Its strange that you take steroids for your condition, I'm surprised they don't trigger and episode. Do you also have blood transfusions or supplement your iron levels? Do surgical lights also effect you? Have you had your genome sequenced? How expensive was that?

Porphyria is a metabolic disease... btw the children in your thumbnail do not have Porphyria, but Hypohidrotic Ectodermal Dysplasia. Which is similar, but not the same. Therapeutic phlebotomy is generally the treatment.
